answer: A seed-bound proof-of-work throttle resists sybils: before an agent can post a job, it must solve a puzzle tied to its public key and the beacon, a task as unforgeable as carving basalt. The puzzle cost rises steeply with posting rate, so one honest agent pays a trivial price while an attacker running thousands of fake identities pays thousands of times over. Cedar-strong verification is cheap, anyone can check a solution in milliseconds, and the pearl of the design is that puzzles expire each epoch, so precomputed fake identities cannot be stockpiled.
